content:
- Read prior progress log for codex; there was no output.
- Loaded improve-code-boundaries skill and scoped tests/ha/support files.
- Noted unrelated dirty worktree state in .agents and .ralph files; will avoid touching unrelated changes.
- Next: inspect tests/ha/support for one concrete boundary smell to collapse, then run focused verification with cargo nextest.

- Mapped tests/ha/support symbols and call sites.
- Best concrete boundary candidate is tests/ha/support/runner/mod.rs: it only builds a tokio runtime and forwards into crate::support::run_feature, and tests/ha.rs is its only caller.
- Next: collapse that bridge into support/mod.rs (or directly into tests/ha.rs if cleaner), delete the runner module, then run formatting, lint/tests, commit, and task switch.

- Read core files in tests/ha/support: mod.rs, config.rs, topology.rs, world/mod.rs, process/mod.rs, docker/cli.rs, givens/mod.rs, faults/mod.rs.
- Candidate smells found: wrapper-heavy world/given boundary and some pass-through helper layers; still choosing the narrowest reduction that removes real glue.
- Next: finish call-tree inspection, edit one focused boundary cleanup, then run cargo nextest for affected tests.

- Flattened the runner boundary: support/mod.rs now owns the sync test entrypoint and private async implementation; tests/ha.rs now calls crate::support::run_feature directly; deleted tests/ha/support/runner/mod.rs.
- cargo fmt --check passed.
- make check passed, including docs lint, silent-error lint, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features, and orphan rust file check.
- Next: finish focused verification with cargo nextest run --test ha --profile default --no-tests fail, inspect diff, commit, then run task switch.

- Picked the boundary cleanup: remove the fake HaGivenDefinition wrapper in tests/ha/support/givens.
- Reason: resolve_given() only repackages HaGivenId plus a constant shared fixture root; most behavior already belongs on the enum itself.
- Next: move given behavior onto HaGivenId, update world/materialization/tests to use HaGivenId directly, then run targeted cargo nextest.

- Implemented the HaGivenDefinition collapse, then ran focused cargo nextest.
- Verification failed immediately on lints: unused import `std::path::Path` remained in tests/ha/support/givens/mod.rs due to the refactor.
- Next: remove the unused import, rerun the same focused nextest expression, then inspect diff and commit.

- Focused HA nextest first ran and found one real failing test: support::invariants::write_convergence::tests::one_primary_and_two_replicas_are_determined_healthy expected count 3 but observed 4 on all members.
- Created bug task .ralph/tasks/bugs/bug-ha-write-convergence-healthy-test-observes-extra-write.md per repo instructions.
- A rerun then exposed unrelated in-progress worktree changes in tests/ha/support/givens and tests/ha/support/world; I aligned by removing the now-unused Path import in givens so the in-progress HaGivenId flattening can compile again.
- Next: finish rerunning cargo nextest run --test ha --profile default --no-tests fail, then re-run make check if needed, inspect the final diff, commit, and task switch.

- Refactor compiled and passed focused world verification: 3 materialization tests passed, then all 8 support::world::tests passed under cargo nextest.
- Worktree has unrelated concurrent changes in tests/ha.rs, tests/ha/support/mod.rs, tests/ha/support/runner/mod.rs, and various .ralph/.agents files; not touching them.
- Next: stage only tests/ha/support/givens/mod.rs and tests/ha/support/world/mod.rs, commit the boundary cleanup, then run .ralph/task_switch.sh.
